Declare assumptions for interval-constrained sensitivity completion

Source: R/spec.R
catmech_spec.Rd

The interval convention is [a,b] for the first category and (a,b] for subsequent categories. Finite endpoints may define a restricted domain. The probability is a sensitivity weight for replacing flagged, in-bound observed values, not an estimated posterior corruption probability.

Usage

catmech_spec(
  value,
  category,
  levels,
  thresholds,
  flag = NULL,
  flag_yes = "Yes",
  flag_no = "No",
  corruption_probability = NULL,
  conflict_policy = c("error", "reconstruct"),
  min_donors = 1L,
  n_donors = 5L,
  fallback = c("error", "normal")
)

Arguments

value, category

Names of the continuous measurement and interval category.

levels

Ordered, unique category labels.

thresholds

Strictly increasing numeric endpoints, length levels + 1.

flag

Optional quality-flag column name; NULL means no flags.

flag_yes, flag_no

Labels for suspect and non-suspect flags. Missing flags do not mark an observed value as suspect; this is an explicit assumption.

corruption_probability

Fixed scalar replacement probability in [0,1]. Must be supplied explicitly when a flag column is configured. With no flag, NULL is normalized to zero.

conflict_policy

Either "error" or "reconstruct". The latter declares the category authoritative for all observed category/value conflicts.

min_donors

Minimum eligible donors before using the fallback policy.

n_donors

Number of nearest eligible donors from which to sample.

fallback

"error" (default) or "normal" for an explicit, experimental truncated-normal fallback when too few category donors exist.

Value

A validated catmech_spec list.

Examples

spec <- catmech_spec("value", "band", c("low", "high"), c(-Inf, 0, Inf))
spec$conflict_policy
#> [1] "error"
